description: For each throwing hand, count award records. Then keep the hands whose share of the total is above the average share, and summarise them.

c.request: Using `player_award` matched to `player` (dropping awards with no matching player), tally the award winners by throwing hand (`player.throws`). Treat a blank or missing hand as its own group. Work out each hand's share of the total across all hands. Keep only the hands whose share is above the average share. For those hands, give a single row with three values: the total of their tallies, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round anything. For each throwing hand, count award records. Then keep the hands whose share of the total is above the average share, and summarise them.
c.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '') AS hand, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_award pa JOIN player p ON pa.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '')), s AS (SELECT hand, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT hand, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_tally, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

b.request: Count the award records in `player_award` for each throwing hand (`player.throws`, with blank or missing as its own group, and awards with no matching player dropped). Compute each hand's share of the total, keep only the hands whose share is above the average share, and return one row with the sum of their counts, their average share, and their average excess over the average share, all unrounded
b.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws), ''), '') AS hand, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_award pa JOIN player p ON pa.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY 1), s AS (SELECT hand, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s, a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

a.request: Matching each `player_award` record to its player in `player` (dropping awards with no matching player), count the award records for each throwing hand (`player.throws`), so a player with several awards counts once per award. Treat a blank or missing hand as its own group. Work out each hand's share of the total count across all hands. Keep only the hands whose share is above the average share across hands. For those hands, give a single row with three values: the total of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws),''),'') AS h, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_award a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY 1), s AS (SELECT h, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), t AS (SELECT h, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share_of_selected, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM t WHERE share > avg_share

d.request: Using `player_award` matched to `player` (dropping awards with no matching player), count the award records for each throwing hand (`player.throws`), treating a blank or missing hand as its own group. Work out each hand's share of the total count across all hands, and keep only the hands whose share is above the average share across all hands. For those hands, give a single row with three values: the total of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds the average share. Don't round anything.
d.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.throws),''),'(blank)') AS hand, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM player_award pa JOIN player p ON pa.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY 1), s AS (SELECT hand, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
